title: 2027 Kia Sportage Hybrid: Prices, Reviews & Pictures - CarGurus.com
summary: Explore the 2027 Kia Sportage Hybrid with CarGurus reviews, pricing insights, comparisons, news and expert analysis.
body_markdown:
## Look & feel


8/10


The 2027 Kia Sportage Hybrid is available in LX, S, EX, X-Line, and SX Prestige trim levels. The new FWD models for the 2027 model year are the S and EX, which offer all-wheel drive (AWD) as a $1,600 option. The X-Line and SX Prestige continue to include AWD as standard equipment. The LX base model remains FWD-only.


Across the range, prices span $32,085–$42,185, including the $1,495 destination charge. Our test vehicle had SX Prestige trim and carpeted floor mats, bringing the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) to $42,385. That’s over $2,000 less than a Honda CR-V Sport Touring Hybrid or Toyota RAV4 Limited.


Kia updated the Sportage’s styling for 2026, cleaning it up and making the SUV more appealing. Heritage Blue paint also debuted last year, and everyone we spoke to about the test car liked the color. It hides dust and dirt well, too.


Inside, the SX Prestige features a premium grade of Kia’s SynTex artificial leather upholstery. It's convincing enough, and features classy, simulated suede on the upper seatbacks with this trim level. Choose the Misty Gray over Saturn Black color, and the light and bright interior has a premium, upscale look and feel. This trim level’s panoramic glass sunroof also contributes to the airy sensation.


That Misty Gray color, used on the hard plastic lower dashboard, console, and door panels, likely also reduces gloss in those areas, further elevating the cabin's quality. Not that it needs much help in that area. Polished metallic detailing, sophisticated design, and advanced technology all ensure the SX Prestige appears to be a class above.


Controls are laid out in an intuitive fashion, with one exception. Under the center air vents, there is a dual-function, touch-sensing panel with two control knobs. Drivers can use this panel to operate the radio and infotainment system, or for the climate controls. We found it was possible to lose track of which set of controls is active at a given time, which can cause confusion. One way around that is leaving the climate panel active and using voice commands or steering wheel controls for audio functions.


## Performance


7/10


Kia’s hybrid powertrain is remarkably satisfying for daily drivability. It consists of a 1.6-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine, an electric motor, a starter-generator motor, and a 1.49-kWh battery pack to generate 232 horsepower and 271 pound-feet of torque. Kia also uses a traditional six-speed automatic transmission to get the power to the ground, instead of a continuously variable transmission (CVT) or other solution.


As a result, the Sportage Hybrid accelerates quickly from a stop thanks to the electric motor’s instant torque, and it doesn’t groan or drone due to Kia’s use of a conventional automatic transmission. This setup eliminates any turbo lag or CVT laziness. Even in the Eco driving mode, which we used almost exclusively, the Sportage Hybrid feels plenty zippy. Other modes include Sport and configurable My Drive settings, and with AWD there is a Terrain menu with Snow, Mud, and Sand to better leverage the 8.3 inches of ground clearance.


FWD models are EPA-rated at 41 mpg combined, which is better than a Honda CR-V Hybrid with FWD but worse than a similar Toyota RAV4. Our SX Prestige test vehicle had standard AWD, and as we often find with hybrids, it fell short of the expectations set by its EPA fuel economy rating of 35 mpg combined (already lower than an equivalent CR-V or RAV4).


During a week behind the wheel, we put almost 650 miles on the test vehicle while roaming all over Southern California. Our average was 32.6 mpg, exactly matching what the Sportage Hybrid returned on our mountainous test-vehicle evaluation loop. However, that number beat the Honda CR-V Hybrid (32.4 mpg) and Mazda CX-50 Hybrid (30.2 mpg) on the same testing route.


Soft, springy suspension emphasizes ride quality, so drivers should take speed humps and pavement dips with care. Nevertheless, the Sportage Hybrid is agreeable to drive in the city, the suburbs, and on the freeway. The steering doesn’t distinguish itself, which is as it should be in a vehicle like this, and the brake pedal feels good.


Undulating mountain roads revealed a few weaknesses. On smaller cracks and ripples in the pavement, the Sportage Hybrid’s ride seemed firm and busy. On whoops and dips, it felt bouncy with too much body motion, and some lateral movement was sudden and unexpected. For this situation, it seems as though the suspension is tuned to the opposite of what drivers would want.


The weakest link regarding handling was the P235/55R19 Hankook Dynapro tires. They were very unhappy on a winding road, but contribute to a quiet ride on highways, so they’re probably a good choice for an SUV like this.


## Form & function


9/10


Kia equips the Sportage Hybrid SX Prestige with numerous comfort and convenience features, including dual-zone automatic climate control, a heated steering wheel, heated and ventilated front seats, and heated rear seats. It also has a 10-way power driver’s seat with memory for the seat and mirrors, and an eight-way power front passenger’s seat.


Though the Sportage is two rungs down on the Kia SUV model ladder, we thought the SX Prestige’s driver’s seat was much more comfortable than the one in a **[Telluride X-Pro SX Prestige we tested the week before](https://www.cargurus.com/research/2027-Kia-Telluride-c34461)** . The second-row seat was also comfortable and accommodating, with excellent leg support, legroom, and a proper backrest angle.


The Sportage Hybrid is a roomy vehicle for its segment, and the interior is well-designed, with a lot of storage space. For example, the center console storage tray features deployable cupholders that close for more flexibility. Also, the wireless smartphone charger is hidden inside a covered bin, allowing buyers to store items they’d rather keep from prying eyes.


That level of thoughtfulness continues in the second-row seating area, where the Sportage Hybrid offers grocery bag hooks, front head restraint frames that serve as jacket hangers, and a storage bin perfect for holding a smartphone. Kia also provides seatback pockets, USB charging ports, and air conditioning vents for rear-seat riders. However, the cupholders in the center armrest are quite small.


Most Sportage Hybrid trim levels have a “smart” power liftgate that can sense the proximity of the key fob and automatically open after a few seconds. When the liftgate rises, it reveals up to 39.5 cubic feet of space with the dual-level cargo floor in its lowest setting. The maximum cargo volume measurement is 73.7 cubic feet. Those numbers are among the most generous in the compact SUV segment and even surpass some midsize SUVs. Compared to Kia’s own Sorento Hybrid, at 45 and 75.5 cubic feet behind the second and first rows, respectively, the Sportage Hybrid is nearly as roomy inside.


## Technology


9/10


Every 2027 Kia Sportage Hybrid has a panoramic display containing digital instrumentation. Most trim levels feature static gauges with a 4.2-inch driver display between them, but the SX Prestige trim upgrades to a fully configurable 12.3-inch panel.


All trims feature a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system equipped with wireless Apple CarPlay, wireless Android Auto, and SiriusXM satellite radio. Our SX Prestige test vehicle also had Kia Connect connected services with a three-year complimentary trial subscription, including voice recognition, over-the-air navigation system updates, access to a Wi-Fi hotspot, digital key functionality, and more.


The tech is very approachable and easy to use, especially the voice recognition system, which is quick to respond to commands and does so accurately. Truly, it is a joy to use. We also used the wireless Apple CarPlay extensively and had no trouble with it. Apple Music selections streamed through the SX Prestige’s standard Harman Kardon audio system sounded terrific.


A head-up display is standard on the SX Prestige and shows the driver when other vehicles are in their blind spot, as well as other pertinent information. Another extremely helpful feature is Leading Vehicle Departure Alert, which notifies the driver when vehicles ahead have started moving again. This is useful for those who tend to check their phones while sitting at intersections or in heavy commuter traffic.


Among the changes for the 2027 model year is a new X-Line Technology Package, which allows buyers to pair that trim level’s trendy blacked-out appearance with the 12.3-inch digital instrumentation panel, navigation system, and Harman Kardon audio system previously found only on the SX Prestige.


## Safety


8/10


The 2027 Sportage Hybrid includes numerous standard driver-assistance features, including high-beam assist, forward-collision warning with pedestrian and cyclist detection, automatic emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, lane-departure warning, lane-keep assist, lane-centering assist, and intersection braking assistance. However, shoppers have to upgrade from the LX to the S trim level for blind-spot monitors and rear cross-traffic alert.


The new-for-2027 X-Line Technology Package adds a surround-view camera system, blind-spot cameras, Highway Driving Assist, side parking sensors, and reverse automatic braking to the X-Line trim level. Those features are standard on the SX Prestige, along with steering assist for the blind-spot monitors, lane-change assist, oncoming vehicle collision avoidance, automatic curve speed reduction, safe-exit assist, and Remote Smart Parking Assist.


Highway Driving Assist combines the adaptive cruise control and lane-centering assist for a greater degree of automation while driving on highways. Its refinement and accuracy are impressive, and even more so thanks to a hands-on-detection steering wheel that’s more convenient than other driver-attention-monitoring methods.


However, when Highway Driving Assist wasn’t active, the lane-keeping systems kept trying to divert us into left turn lanes when the painted lines to the left branched away. We also found that the curve speed reduction feature reduced speed a bit too abruptly.


Remote Smart Parking Assist allows drivers to stand outside of the Sportage Hybrid and, using the key fob, command the SUV to drive itself forward or backward into and out of tight parking spaces. In the U.S. market, the need for this feature is less obvious, but in other parts of the world, it can be a technology an owner might use daily.


In crash testing, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration gave the Sportage Hybrid a five-star overall rating, with five-star ratings for each individual assessment except rollover resistance, where the Kia earned four stars.


The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety named the Sportage a Top Safety Pick+, its highest safety award. That applies to 2027 models as well.


## Cost-effectiveness


8/10


With a starting price just over $32,000, a fuel economy rating as high as 41 mpg combined, and 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain and five-year/60,000-mile basic warranty coverage, the 2027 Kia Sportage Hybrid is a cost-effective choice. Add its roomy interior, impressive technology, and favorable safety ratings, and it just makes good sense as a purchase.


Fortunately, the Sportage Hybrid’s appeal extends beyond practical matters. The turbocharged hybrid powertrain provides satisfying acceleration and competitive real-world fuel economy, the interior is comfortable and stylish, and Kia offers features that aren’t found in many other vehicles regardless of price, let alone in this class. Plus, buyers get three years of free Kia Connect services, so it isn't hard to recommend it.
